text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Newly-elected deputies of the National Assembly (lower house) took oath of office completing the first phase of the protocol for the transfer of power to the new Parliament.
- Pakistan Muslim Leaque (PML) party has agreed to make Mian Shahbaz Sharif, younger brother of prime minister in-waiting Nawaz Sharif, chief minister of Punjab province.
- Nawaz Sharif has said he would avoid political confrontation in order to focus on rehabilitating the economy.
- The Mohajir National Movement (MQM) is set to join the Pakistan Muslim League as coalition partner in the federal and Sindh provincial governments.
- A Christian demonstrator shot during a protest in Karachi on Thursday died in hospital.

- A two-member European Commission team is arriving on Thursday for on-the-spot verification of prices and export documents of five textile mills selected for anti-dumping proceedings initiated by the Commission against Pakistan and other countries.
- Pakistan's liquid forex reserves increased to $797 million after obtaining a three-year $160 million loan from the Bank of China, sources said.
- Pakistan's caretaker government has ordered television and radio to be opened up to multiple private broadcasters, Information Minister Irshad Ahmad Haqqani said.
- The caretaker government announced removal of limitation on the profitability of the country's oil refineries placed in the Petroleum Policy of 1994.
- Pakistan may import up to 100 tonnes of gold by the end of 1997, the Gold Importers Association said.
- Benazir Bhutto said her Pakistan People's Party would strive to end confrontational politics.
